title: ProposalCheck: the lint and its limits
summary: ProposalCheck rejects ADDRESS, CALL, INTERPRET, SIGNAL, PULL, directives, stream functions, VALUE(), Sys* functions, dot names other than .Array/.ShellCollection, reflection messages (~class ~send ~setMethod ~launch ~execute ~poll ...), RESULT/RC/SIGL as variables, bare string commands, calls to unknown methods, and code with no RETURN. It is a lint, not a sandbox; it stays because the security manager does not see built-in classes (.File, .Stream) or value(..., ENVIRONMENT).
authority: built and tested (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-24)
invariants: The lint is early feedback plus cover for what the security manager cannot see
A rejected proposal is never run, by a person or by autopilot
procedure: Extend the lint when a new built-in route to I/O is found
